review_notes: I read the whole file and the definition of `localMultiplicity`/`localMultiplicity_def` in LocalMultiplicity.lean. I grepped the repo for uses of the two lemmas below. I found no rewrite cycles and no bad orientations. The existing simp lemmas (`localMultiplicity_onePointMap_pow_zero`, `..._infty`, `coe_spherePow`, `degree_onePointMap_pow`) look sound. The two findings are about missing simp coverage, and both are minor. I could not run Lean, so I don't know whether simp would actually fire or discharge the side conditions as expected. Whether the chart lemma is a good simp lemma depends on how `invChart` and `OnePoint.map` simp lemmas interact with it, and I did not check that.

findings.problem: The `0` and `∞` multiplicities are `@[simp]`, but the third case, multiplicity `1` at a finite nonzero point, is not. The three lemmas together give the full local-multiplicity computation for this map, so the simp set is incomplete. Downstream, `branchValues_spherePow_subset` has to pass the lemma by hand (`simp [localMultiplicity_onePointMap_pow_coe_of_ne_zero hn hz] at hx`) instead of relying on the simp set.
findings.proposed_change: Mark it `@[simp]`. The hypotheses `hn : n ≠ 0` and `hz : z ≠ 0` are plain side conditions that simp can discharge from hypotheses in context. The LHS has a head symbol and shape like the other two simp lemmas, and the RHS is the literal `1`, so there is no loop risk. Then the call at line 160 can be `simp [hn, hz] at hx`.
findings.benefit: Callers can compute the multiplicity of the power map at any point by simp alone. The simp interface becomes uniform across the three cases, and the explicit lemma instantiation in the branch-value proof goes away.

findings.excerpt:
theorem invChart_onePointMap_pow_invChart_symm (hn : n ≠ 0) (w : ℂ) :
    invChart (OnePoint.map (fun z : ℂ ↦ z ^ n) (invChart.symm w)) = w ^ n := by
findings.problem: This is the canonical chart-expression normalisation (`invChart ∘ map ∘ invChart.symm = (· ^ n)`). It is not tagged simp, so each client passes it to simp by hand: `simpa [localMultiplicity_def, invChart_onePointMap_pow_invChart_symm hn, zero_pow hn]`. The lemma is stated with a side condition `hn` and a pattern that unfolding `localMultiplicity_def` produces.
findings.proposed_change: Consider adding `@[simp]` to this lemma. The side condition `n ≠ 0` is dischargeable and the RHS `w ^ n` is strictly simpler, so there is no cycle. The `simpa` at line 126 could then drop the explicit argument, apart from supplying `hn`. This depends on the simp-normal form of the LHS after other `invChart` and `OnePoint.map` simp lemmas have fired. If those rewrite the LHS first, keep the lemma non-simp.
findings.benefit: Chart computations for `OnePoint.map (· ^ n)` at `∞` would close by `simp [hn]`. Later files would not need to rediscover and pass the lemma explicitly.
